skill.name: nano-banana-2
skill.description: Generate images with Google Nano Banana 2 (Gemini-family flash-tier text-to-image) on RunComfy — bundled with the model's documented prompting patterns so the skill gets sharper output than naive prompting against the same model. Documents Nano Banana 2's strengths (rapid iteration, in-image typography rendering, predictable framing, optional web-grounded context), the resolution-tier pricing, the safety-tolerance dial, and when to route to Nano Banana Pro / GPT Image 2 / Flux 2 / Seedream instead. Calls `runcomfy run google/nano-banana-2/text-to-image` through the local RunComfy CLI. Triggers on "nano banana", "nano-banana-2", "nano banana 2", "google image gen", "gemini image", or any explicit ask to generate with this model.
skill.summary: Generate still images with Nano Banana 2 through RunComfy, with prompt guidance, model routing, and CLI settings.
skill.author: agentspace-so

security_audit.summary: Most static findings were Markdown formatting, schema field names, documentation links, or sample prompts rather than executable code. Confirmed risks are the intended RunComfy CLI execution, setup/login commands, and disclosed outbound RunComfy API and download behavior; no prompt injection attempt or hidden exfiltration intent was found.

remediation.suggestion: Require user confirmation before running runcomfy, npx, or npm commands. JSON-encode prompt values and avoid direct shell interpolation.
Clearly disclose that prompts and optional web-search context are sent to RunComfy. Ask before sending sensitive or private content.
Prefer RUNCOMFY_TOKEN in CI and never print or inspect the token file. Document least-privilege token handling for shared machines.

content.value_statement: Image teams need fast drafts, platform formats, and reliable text rendering. This skill guides Nano Banana 2 prompts and RunComfy CLI settings.
actual_capabilities: Routes text-to-image requests to the RunComfy Nano Banana 2 model endpoint.
Documents controls for image count, seed, aspect ratio, resolution, format, safety tolerance, and web search.
Provides prompt patterns for subject-first scenes, quoted in-image text, and seed-locked refinement.
Explains when to choose Nano Banana 2, Nano Banana Edit, Nano Banana Pro, GPT Image 2, Flux 2, or Seedream.
Summarizes RunComfy CLI prerequisites, exit codes, output handling, and security notes.
limitations: It generates still images only and does not edit images or create video.
It requires the RunComfy CLI, a RunComfy account, and either login or a token.
Prompts are sent to the RunComfy Model API, and web search may add external context.
Each request supports up to four outputs, and higher resolutions add cost and latency.

use_cases.title: Create social thumbnail batches
use_cases.description: Generate four fast draft options with platform-specific ratios before selecting a final direction.

use_cases.title: Draft branded text visuals
use_cases.description: Use quoted text and placement guidance to improve posters, product cards, and launch graphics.

use_cases.title: Explore current-event imagery
use_cases.description: Enable web grounding only when prompts need current entities, events, or public context.

prompt_templates.title: Basic Image Draft
prompt_templates.prompt: Generate one Nano Banana 2 image for this concept: [describe subject, setting, mood, and style]. Use the default 1K square output.

prompt_templates.title: Batch Concept Round
prompt_templates.prompt: Create four Nano Banana 2 drafts for [campaign or asset]. Use [aspect ratio], 0.5K resolution, and keep the subject consistent across variants.

prompt_templates.title: Typography Asset
prompt_templates.scenario: Produce an image with visible text.
prompt_templates.prompt: Generate a [poster/card/banner] with the exact text "[text]" placed [position]. Specify font style, contrast, subject, background, and aspect ratio.

prompt_templates.title: Seeded Final Pass
prompt_templates.scenario: Refine a selected direction for final delivery.
prompt_templates.prompt: Refine this selected Nano Banana 2 direction using seed [number], [2K or 4K] resolution, [aspect ratio], and these changes: [specific visual changes].

output_examples.input: Create four vertical launch-image options for a wellness tea campaign.
output_examples.output: Recommended setup: four images, 9:16 ratio, 0.5K resolution for quick review. Prompt focus: one ceramic teacup, morning light, quoted headline text, and uncluttered composition.

output_examples.input: Make a final 16:9 product card with the headline Brewed Quietly.
output_examples.output: Recommended setup: one image, 16:9 ratio, 2K resolution, and a fixed seed. Prompt focus: centered product, precise headline placement, clean studio light, and balanced negative space.

output_examples.input: Create an image about a public event from this week.
output_examples.output: Recommended setup: enable web grounding only for this current-event request. Confirm that the prompt may be sent to RunComfy with added latency and cost.

best_practices: Front-load the subject, action, environment, style, and camera details in that order.
Quote exact in-image text and specify its placement, contrast, and font style.
Lock the seed when refining a selected composition across small prompt changes.
anti_patterns: Do not use this endpoint for image edits that must preserve a real subject identity.
Do not combine many conflicting style anchors in one prompt.
Do not enable web search unless the image needs current real-world context.

faq.question: What does this skill generate?
faq.answer: It generates still images with Nano Banana 2 through the RunComfy Model API.

faq.question: Does it require a RunComfy account?
faq.answer: Yes. You need the RunComfy CLI and either runcomfy login or a RUNCOMFY_TOKEN value.

faq.question: Can it edit existing images?
faq.answer: No. The skill points image-edit requests to the separate Nano Banana Edit workflow.

faq.question: How many images can it request at once?
faq.answer: The documented endpoint supports one to four images per request.

faq.question: When should web search be enabled?
faq.answer: Enable it only for prompts that depend on current events, real entities, or fresh public context.

faq.question: Can Claude, Codex, or Claude Code use it?
faq.answer: Yes. The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
